top10.introHtml: Top 10 picks for a cheap fun second car — 4-seat convertibles within 35 miles of Media, PA, $7k–$15k. Ranked on condition first, then reliability, mileage, and value. No 2-seat roadsters. Refreshed daily.

picks.whyGood: Verified clean title and zero accidents on a 70k-mile E93 BMW 328i — one of the best condition-per-dollar packages on the list. The E93 3-series convertible is a proven, parts-abundant platform with strong regional dealer support. Under $10k with nearly every reliability box ticked.
picks.whatToVerify: Operate the power soft-top through 3 full open/close cycles; check headliner and rear carpet for water staining. Inspect the N52 engine for coolant leaks and valve-cover gasket seep. Check front subframe for rust. Ask for full service history — specifically timing chain tensioner record if over 120k total miles.
picks.bottomLine: Strong E93 BMW at a fair price — verified condition badges make this the safest bet on the list.

picks.whyGood: The E46 330Ci is widely considered one of BMW's greatest driver's cars — naturally aspirated 3.0L inline-6, near-perfect weight distribution, and sharp handling that still impresses today. 65k miles with clean title and no accidents at $10k is genuinely rare. The enthusiast pick on the list.
picks.whatToVerify: E46 specific: check subframe reinforcement plates (critical — ask if already done), VANOS rattle on cold start, and soft-top hydraulic pump operation and rear window seam for leaks. Oil pan gasket and rear main seal are common slow seeps. Note: ~38mi from 19063 — just outside the 35mi target; confirm the drive distance works.
picks.bottomLine: If the subframe plates and VANOS check out, this is the most rewarding driver on the entire list.

picks.whyGood: Only 9 miles from Media — the closest BMW on the list. 80k miles on a late E93 328i is a comfortable starting point for years of service without major surgery. Sky Motor Cars in West Chester is a known local independent European dealer, easy to revisit for any follow-up.
picks.whatToVerify: No condition badges on this listing — budget for an independent pre-purchase inspection at a local BMW specialist. E93 checklist: soft-top operation, N52 oil leaks, coolant expansion tank, subframe inspection, transmission fluid condition.
picks.bottomLine: Best location on the list — local pickup makes this an easy no-pressure first look.

picks.whyGood: Two miles from Media — you could walk to the test drive. 65k miles on a W209 CLK350, one of Mercedes' most elegant and lasting coupe-convertible designs. The 3.5L V6 is a proven, smooth unit that's largely trouble-free at this mileage with proper service.
picks.whatToVerify: W209 CLK: check soft-top for tears and listen for hydraulic pump hesitation during operation. Rear window is plastic — inspect carefully for yellowing or crazing (costly to replace). Check for any active SRS or ESP warning lights. Pull a VIN report to verify no undisclosed accidents.
picks.bottomLine: Closest car on the list — German elegance at a price that leaves room in the budget.

picks.whyGood: Great Deal badge, verified clean title, zero accidents. The B7 S4 Cabriolet pairs a 4.2L V8 339hp engine with quattro AWD — possibly the most exotic powertrain available under $15k in a 4-seat drop-top. At $7,204 this is the most dramatic bargain on the list if mechanical health checks out.
picks.whatToVerify: CRITICAL B7 S4 check: timing chain, water pump (chain-driven), and tensioner service history. If unserviced, this repair runs $2,500–$4,000 — ask for documentation before scheduling the test drive. Also check convertible top motor function, HVAC control module (common fault), and the MMI screen.
picks.bottomLine: The V8 sound alone justifies the drive — but the timing chain service record is a hard pass/fail criterion.

picks.whyGood: Newest car in the Top 10 at only 10 years old with verified clean title and no accidents. The A3 Cabriolet's 1.8T engine paired with the S tronic transmission is a refined, well-supported powertrain. Modern safety features, comfortable ride, easy to daily-drive.
picks.whatToVerify: DSG/S tronic clutch pack wear check (any hesitation or shudder at low speeds is a flag). 3-layer soft-top: inspect seam stitching and rear window for delamination. Check A-pillar drains for leaf/debris blockage — a common water ingress path. Pull a full CarFax to cross-check the no-accidents badge.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern pick on the list — latest tech, comfortable daily driver, worry-free mechanically if the transmission checks out.

picks.whyGood: Verified clean title and no accidents on a B8 S5 Cabriolet with the 3.0T supercharged V6 (333hp). The B8 generation ditched the V8 timing chain issues entirely — the supercharged V6 is a significantly more reliable powertrain. Under $11k for a supercharged quattro drop-top is outstanding value.
picks.whatToVerify: Supercharger belt and bearing inspection, rear differential fluid service, Haldex clutch fluid (AWD models), and electro-hydraulic convertible top hydraulic line check (look for seeping fluid under the rear deck). The B8 is more electronically complex — verify all MMI and HVAC functions work correctly.
picks.bottomLine: More modern and mechanically sounder than the V8 S4 — the supercharged V6 is the right engine choice.

picks.whyGood: Cars.com 'Great Deal' badge, zero accidents, clean title on a 66k-mile Chrysler 200S Convertible under $10k. The 200S trim adds sport tuning and appearance upgrades. The Pentastar 3.6L V6 (if equipped) is one of Chrysler's most reliable modern engines with cheap and plentiful parts.
picks.whatToVerify: Verify it has the 3.6L V6 (not the 2.4L I4). Note: listed at ~41 miles from Media — just outside the 35mi radius, so confirm the drive is acceptable before making the trip. Check convertible top operation and rear window defogging grid; fabric tops on these are known to develop tears near the header.
picks.bottomLine: Best-rated deal on cars.com — verify the distance works and inspect that top carefully.

picks.whyGood: Cheapest car in the Top 10 with both a verified clean title and no-accidents badge. BMW's N52 inline-6 in the 128i is legendarily durable — 147k miles is entirely normal for this engine with consistent oil changes. The E88 1-series cabriolet is a compact, athletic drop-top that punches above its price.
picks.whatToVerify: High miles: check the soft-top hydraulic pump seals (pump lives under the rear deck — listen for hesitation or look for drips), coolant expansion tank (plastic, known to crack with age on high-mileage units), and valley gasket oil seep at the rear of the engine. A PPI at any independent BMW shop in the area is strongly recommended at 147k.
picks.bottomLine: Least expensive BMW with verified condition — the N52 is nearly indestructible with regular oil changes.

picks.whyGood: 33,887 original miles on a 1994 Pontiac Firebird Formula Convertible — time-capsule territory. Verified clean title, no accidents. The Formula trim came with the 5.7L LT1 V8 (275hp), the same engine as the Corvette of the era. At 33k miles this car has barely been broken in.
picks.whatToVerify: Verify the engine (Formula should have the LT1 V8 — confirm). Inspect rubber seals, weatherstripping, and soft-top fabric — even lightly used rubber deteriorates with age over 30 years. Check brake lines and fuel lines for age-related deterioration, test all electrical systems (window motors, gauges, A/C), and confirm there are no ethanol-related fuel system issues from long storage.
picks.bottomLine: A genuine time capsule at the top of the budget — if the LT1 V8 checks out, this is the most unique car on the list.

mustangs.introHtml: Ford Mustang convertibles (2005+) found in this refresh — S197 and S550 generations only. Ranked by trim, mileage, and proximity to Media, PA.

picks.whyGood: GT Premium trim with the 4.6L V8 (300hp) — the right trim for a Mustang. Only 43k miles, verified clean title, no accidents, sold by Tom Masano Ford. The 2005–2009 S197 GT started the modern Mustang revival and the 4.6 3V V8 sounds exactly right.
picks.whatToVerify: S197 soft-top: check rear seat water staining from top seal failure (very common), test rear window defogging. 4.6L 3V V8: verify the plastic intake manifold crossover tube hasn't cracked (cold-start coolant leak). Rear axle clunk on takeoff is a known issue. Note: ~40mi from Media, just outside the 35mi radius.
picks.bottomLine: Best Mustang on the list — GT V8 at 43k miles is rare. Confirm the roof seals are sound.

picks.whyGood: Only 9 miles from Media — the most convenient Mustang on the list. The V6 Convertible trim at $10,459 leaves room in the budget. Late S197 generation (2010–2014 refresh) with updated front fascia and improved interior over the early cars.
picks.whatToVerify: V6 engine — verify it's the 3.7L V6 (305hp, not the older 4.0L). Test soft-top full operation, check rear seat for water damage, rear window defogging. Ask about any open recalls. CarFax recommended — dealer information is not listed so source context is limited.
picks.bottomLine: Closest Mustang to Media at the lowest price — quick local test drive possible.

picks.whyGood: Sixth-gen S550 Mustang (2015–2023) — the most modern generation, bringing independent rear suspension for the first time. Premium trim, 26 miles from Media in Berlin NJ. The S550 represents a major step forward in refinement and handling over the S197.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm engine: V8 5.0L is strongly preferred for character; at this mileage (141k) and price a 2.3 EcoBoost is more likely but check. IRS bushing and wheel bearing inspection at 141k. Soft-top: the S550 top is more robust than S197 but still check all seals and rear window.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern Mustang generation available — IRS and updated chassis make it the best daily driver of the bunch.

picks.whyGood: Cheapest Mustang on the list at $9,995, sold by Keyser Miller Ford in Collegeville — a Ford dealer. The 2014 S197 is the last of the live-rear-axle generation — pure old-school Mustang feel at a budget entry point.
picks.whatToVerify: No listing photo available — visit the dealer in person before deciding. High miles at 148k: thorough inspection needed. Verify engine (V6 or V8). Check soft-top rear seal and rear seats for water damage, rear axle clunk on takeoff. Ask for all service records.
picks.bottomLine: Budget pick at a Ford dealer — high mileage and no photo mean this needs a hands-on inspection first.

picks.whyGood: Newest Mustang on the list at just 6 years old with the EcoBoost Premium trim — Sync 3, B&O audio, leather. The 2.3L EcoBoost makes 310hp and the 10-speed auto is the most modern powertrain available here. Still within extended warranty range for many powertrain components.
picks.whatToVerify: EcoBoost: check intercooler hoses and charge-air system for any delamination or boost leaks. 132k miles on a 2020 is high mileage — pull a full CarFax/AutoCheck report and check for any recall or warranty claims. IRS bushing inspection. Soft-top seals check.
picks.bottomLine: Newest and highest-mileage — modern tech at a high-mile price. Inspect the history carefully.
